subtitle: "Let Amber inspect the model before blaming the solver"

  env: ["JULIA_PROJECT=../../.."]

```{julia}
#| include: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate("../..")
using Amber
```

Circuit simulation failures are often modeling failures. Amber separates
structural checks from numerical convergence so the first error can name the
actual circuit object involved.

## Missing electrical reference

```{julia}
@circuit MissingReference begin
    a = node()
    b = node()
    R1 = resistor(a, b; value=1kΩ)
end

println(explain(MissingReference()))
```

Every electrical circuit needs an absolute reference. Add `ground()` at the
top level and connect the intended reference network to it.

## A floating DC island

```{julia}
@circuit FloatingSensor begin
    gnd = ground()
    sensor_in = node()
    sensor_out = node()
    Reference = resistor(gnd, gnd; value=1kΩ)
    Coupling = capacitor(sensor_in, sensor_out; value=10nF)
end

println(explain(FloatingSensor()))
```

A capacitor relates two voltages but does not establish their absolute DC
level. The diagnostic names the floating nets and suggests a resistive bias or
another finite DC path.

## A misspelled result name

```{julia}
@circuit NamedDivider begin
    gnd = ground()
    input = node()
    output = node()
    Source = voltage_source(input, gnd; dc=1V)
    R1 = resistor(input, output; value=1kΩ)
    R2 = resistor(output, gnd; value=1kΩ)
end

result = operating_point(NamedDivider());

try
    voltage(result, :ouptut)
catch error
    println(sprint(showerror, error))
end
```

Amber suggests close net and device names rather than returning only a raw key
error.

## Invalid analysis settings

```{julia}
try
    transient(NamedDivider(), 1s => 0s)
catch error
    println(sprint(showerror, error))
end
```

The interval is invalid because time must increase. Similar validation applies
to tolerances, frequency grids, time steps, temperatures, and solver options.

## When a solve does not converge

Keep the returned result and ask for its explanation:

```{julia}
result.stats[:converged]
println(explain_failure(result))
```

Then inspect the named dominant residual, realistic parasitics, initial
conditions, and step-size sensitivity. Tightening every tolerance is rarely
the first useful response.
